title: Functorial complex embedding through injective terms
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. There are a functor $M^\bullet\mapsto\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)$ on cochain complexes in $\mathcal A$ (defined as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$) and a natural transformation $j_{M^\bullet}:M^\bullet\to\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)$ such that (1) $j_{M^\bullet}$ is a termwise monomorphism and a quasi-isomorphism (as in [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$), and (2) for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ the map $M^n\to\mathbf N^n(M^\bullet)$ factors through a subobject $I^n\subset\mathbf N^n(M^\bullet)$ which is an injective object of $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: By the functorial injective-embedding theorem [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding], choose a functor $I:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and a natural monomorphism $i:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\to I$ such that every $I(A)$ is injective. For a complex $M^\bullet$ let $J^\bullet(M^\bullet)$ have terms $J^n(M^\bullet)=I(M^n)\oplus I(M^{n+1})$ and differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The maps $i_{M^n}$ and $i_{M^{n+1}}\circ d_M^n$ define a functorial monomorphism of complexes $u_{M^\bullet}:M^\bullet\to J^\bullet(M^\bullet)$, hence a functorial short exact sequence of complexes $0\to M^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}J^\bullet(M^\bullet)\xrightarrow{v}Q^\bullet(M^\bullet)\to0$.

Set $\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)=C(v_{M^\bullet})^\bullet[-1]$, where $v_{M^\bullet}:J^\bullet(M^\bullet)\to Q^\bullet(M^\bullet)$ is the quotient map. Thus $\mathbf N^n(M^\bullet)=Q^{n-1}(M^\bullet)\oplus J^n(M^\bullet)$, with differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-d_Q^{n-1}&-v^n\\0&d_J^n\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The map $j_{M^\bullet}:M^\bullet\to\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)$, $m\mapsto(0,u(m))$, is a natural map of complexes (since $v\circ u=0$) and termwise monic. In degree $n$ it factors through the subobject $I^n=0\oplus J^n(M^\bullet)=0\oplus(I(M^n)\oplus I(M^{n+1}))$, which is injective as a finite direct sum of injective objects. (It does not factor through $I(M^n)\oplus0$ in general, since the second component of $u$ is $i_{M^{n+1}}\circ d_M^n$.)

The quotient complex $\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)/j_{M^\bullet}(M^\bullet)$ identifies degreewise with $Q^{n-1}(M^\bullet)\oplus Q^n(M^\bullet)$, and its differential is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-d_Q^{n-1}&-1\\0&d_Q^n\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, the shifted cone of the identity of $Q^\bullet(M^\bullet)$; the map $h:(q,q')\mapsto(0,-q)$ from degree $n$ to degree $n-1$ (projection to the first summand followed by $-1$ into the second) satisfies $Dh+hD=\mathrm{id}$, so it is a contracting homotopy. Hence the quotient is acyclic. Applying the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to $0\to M^\bullet\xrightarrow{j}\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)\to\mathbf N^\bullet(M^\bullet)/j(M^\bullet)\to0$ shows that $j_{M^\bullet}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. All maps are natural in $M^\bullet$, so $\mathbf N$ and $j$ are functorial.

split_report.summary: Split the item directly along the Stacks lemma-functorial-injective proof. The only non-elementary input is the existing DAG theorem giving a functorial monomorphic embedding into injective objects; the auxiliary complex J, quotient Q, shifted cone N, factorization through an injective summand, and quasi-isomorphism are written as proof steps.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the construction of the functor N with injective subobjects in each degree from the theorem lemma-theorem construction.
